answer: One defence binds each agent identity to a timber structure it must watch. Each seat is a bell tower whose operator glues a registered opal wafer to a floor beam: the wafer's colour drifts as the beam bends with humidity, and a spectroscope reads it against a ferrous tie rod whose rust creep sets a baseline nobody can fake. Each epoch that reading is filed with the clock face; only an unbroken series counts. A sybil farm can't rent one tower a thousand times: every identity needs a real building, a fitted rod and a person on site; cost grows linearly while a new identity inherits no history.
